newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate debt hibernates, LILCOs bid tighter.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate debt hibernates, LILCOs bid tighter.

text.p: A proposed utility merger and failing sentiments for the creator of X-Men comic books gave rise to some jawboning in the U.S. corporate debt markets on Monday, but trade was miniscule and prices flat, dealers said.

Investment-grade spreads were unchanged with a range-bound U.S. Treasury market giving no incentive to trade, dealers said. Even Sunday's announcement of the proposed Long Island Lighting Co/ Brooklyn Union Gas Co merger failed to stir dormant desks, traders said, although LILCO's bonds were bid significantly higher.
LILCO 7-1/8 percent debt was bid 20 basis points tigther.
No markets were seen for Brooklyn Union debt, but traders said any quotes were sure to be sligtly weaker.

The two utilities on Sunday said they agreed to merge in a tax-free stock deal that would create a $4.0 billion electric and gas holding company. The companies also said they will continue talks with the Long Island Power Authority (LIPA) that may lead to the agency's assumption and refinancing of $4.5 billion in LILCO debt via less-costly tax-exempt bonds.
Analysts and buy-siders noted the tone should remain cautiously optimistic, however, until LIPA declares it is active in the restructuring.
The debt is associated with LILCO's Shoreham nuclear power plant, which never opened.

Turning to high-yielders, the stock-backed debt of Marvel Entertainment Group Inc's holding companies slid further on Monday after the companies' Chapter 11 bankruptcy filings on Friday sapped prices.

Marvel Holdings Inc's "old" bonds were bid at 15 compared with a 19 bid on Friday. Trade was essentially non-existent, but some players were on the look-out for vulture fund activity once the new year arrives.
"It's going to be a bloodbath," one trader quipped.

Away from company-specific news, apathy ruled the Street amid holiday-staffed corporate debt desks ahead of the New Year's Day holiday. PSA The Bond Market Trade Association has recommended a 1400 EST/1900 GMT close for U.S. fixed-income markets on Tuesday and a full close on Wednesday.
Primary activity mimicked the comatose secondary in both the investment and high-yield markets.
In the Treasury market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed down 3/32 at 99-13/32 to yield 6.54 percent.
